documents.unit: Office of the AVP for Academic Affairs and Center for Academic Technology
documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Prohibit all use of AI tools
documents.summary: A short memo from the AVP for Academic Affairs and the Center for Academic Technology offering three optional syllabus statements: prohibit, limited and broad use of AI writing tools. Faculty choose; each statement ties violations to the academic misconduct policy.
documents.stance_why: The memo says "there is not a one-size-fits-all approach" and offers three templates, adding "you are not required to use the provided statements", so the university itself sets no stance and delegates to instructors with tiers.

units.why: The memo says "there is not a one-size-fits-all approach" and supplies three statements varying by type of use, so it sets no single rule and lets instructors choose; coded P04 (instructor-level choice), informs, general.
units.anchor: there is not a one-size-fits-all approach to these tools
units.frag_end: vary according to the type of use

units.why: The memo offers three ready-made statements (prohibit, limited, broad) for different kinds of use; this is a set of named levels of AI use, so P05, addressed to instructors choosing a statement before the course.
units.anchor: three separate syllabus statements that vary according to the type of use

units.why: "While you are not required to use the provided statements, we encourage you to consider including a statement" asks faculty to put an AI statement in the syllabus but does not mandate it; P09 fits partly because it is encouraged, not required.
units.anchor: we encourage you to consider including a statement governing the use of these tools
units.frag_start: you are not required to use
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged, but not required, to include a statement governing AI tool use in their syllabi.
units.fit_note: Encouraged rather than required, and the provided wording is optional.

units.why: The first statement says AI tools "are not permitted for any stage or phase of work in this class"; a ban on all AI work in the course is the default-prohibit type P01, addressed to students during work.
units.anchor: not permitted for any stage or phase of work in this class
units.frag_end: phase of work in this class.

units.why: Statement text says use of banned tools "will be considered a violation of the University's academic misconduct policy"; this classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct, P36, in the prohibit option.
units.anchor: your actions will be considered a violation of the University’s academic misconduct policy

units.why: Under the limited option, "there may be opportunities" to use AI writing tools and students are told when, where and how; AI is allowed only for narrow, instructor-specified uses, so P04 (instructor/assignment sets the rule).
units.anchor: You will be informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted

units.why: The limited statement promises "guidance for attribution" when use is permitted, which requires attributing AI use as the instructor directs; P24 is the nearest type though the detail is left to the instructor.
units.frag_start: You will be informed as to
units.policy: Students receive guidance for attribution of permitted AI tool use.
units.fit_note: Only promises guidance on attribution; does not state a disclosure requirement itself.

units.why: "Any use outside of this permission will be considered a violation of the University's academic misconduct policy" sets a fallback of banned unless permitted and treats violations as misconduct; P36 chosen over P06 because the sentence's point is the misconduct classification.
units.anchor: Any use outside of this permission will be considered a violation

units.why: The broad statement says AI writing tools "are welcome in this class" provided use is cited; welcoming AI with a citation condition is permit/encourage by default, P02.
units.anchor: AI writing tools (such as ChatGPT) are welcome in this class

units.why: The condition "provided that you properly cite when and how you use the tool" requires students to cite AI use, P24; P25 does not fit as no tool/prompt detail is named.
units.anchor: provided that you properly cite when and how you use the tool
units.frag_start: are welcome in this class, provided

units.why: "Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as a violation" makes nondisclosure itself the violation, matching P28 (rather than P36, which is about misconduct classification generally).
units.anchor: without proper attribution qualifies as a violation of the University’s academic misconduct policy

units.why: The memo is framed around "AI writing tools, such as ChatGPT" and the statements all say "AI writing tools", limiting scope to writing tools; this scope definition fits P61 partly.
units.policy: The statements cover AI writing tools such as ChatGPT.
units.fit_note: Scope is given by example only; code and other AI tools are not mentioned.

notes: Only one included document; the AI Academic Council policy was not published.
